dna.name: House DNA
dna.description: What runs under every brief that is not Manta's. Defaults, not absolute rules: the project's own brief lines win, and the DNA never relaxes a project's own stricter copy of a DNA ban. Lines marked AI look are the tells of AI-made design that Anthropic's frontend-design skill names (3 Sep 2026), reviewed every six months, next by 14 Apr 2027: add the tells it then names, and drop the ones it no longer names. Lines marked taste are taste bans the founder kept, borrowed rather than his own words: the three words from Manta's brand sheet, the colour line from Chase's taste-vault (mantahostels#3539). A critic reports any DNA miss at P2 at most (#183, #192, #223).
never: AI look: a warm cream ground (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (near #D97757).
AI look: a near-black ground with one bright acid-green or vermilion accent.
AI look: a broadsheet layout of hairline rules, square corners and dense newspaper-like columns.
AI look: the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one corner radius on everything whatever its rank, the same soft grey shadow under each, and gradient washes as decoration.

AI look: template chrome whatever the subject: a tracked-out all-caps eyebrow above every heading; meta strings joined by middle dots (A · B · C); labels built as "WORD — fragment"; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; "→" appended to link and button text.
AI look: a fade-and-slide-up entrance on every section, and a hover transition on every card.
AI look: one word or phrase of a headline accented in italic, bold or another colour; all caps for labels; a label added above content that needs none.
A stock photo of a smiling group; placeholder avatars.
A stock photo used as found, neither chosen nor treated for this page.
Fabricated proof, such as an invented testimonial or client logo: the design vault's gate question vault.proof.
Taste: several colours at equal weight, none dominant.

collections.name: Huge Type, Gallery Layout
collections.description: Very large lettering and a lot of empty white space, with a few gallery-style pictures placed off-centre. The size of the type and the layout carry the look, not decoration.
collections.deployFor: Architects, design studios, portfolios, galleries and arts brands — anyone whose work should look chosen with care.
collections.risk: Let a headline span most of the viewport while a small image interrupts its geometry
collections.imageStyle: editorial image of [SUBJECT], deliberate gallery crop, natural material detail, restrained palette, no typography; build the oversized type and white space in code

collections.name: Clean Page, Product in Front
collections.description: Clean, mostly white pages where the main picture is the product itself — a real screen from the app — set off by one accent colour or a soft background scene.
collections.deployFor: Software and online tools — apps, dashboards and work tools that sell by showing what they do.
collections.risk: Let a single readable product interaction occupy most of the hero
collections.imageStyle: subtle atmospheric background for [SUBJECT], controlled accent palette and calm center, no UI or text; use real screenshots or code for product demonstrations

collections.name: Technical Maps and Data
collections.description: Pages that look like precise instruments: maps, heat-camera and sensor pictures, grid lines and spec sheets, marked with small bright-orange labels, under very large headlines.
collections.deployFor: Mapping, engineering, drones and robotics, scientific tools — any product whose story is measuring things precisely.
collections.risk: Build the page around an annotated visual field with a headline at architectural scale
collections.imageStyle: aerial or sensor-style visualization of [SUBJECT], restrained cinematic contrast, texture and terrain readable, no text or measurements; implement instrument overlays separately in SVG or CSS

collections.name: Glowing Light on Dark
collections.description: Glowing light on a dark background: bright threads and halos of light, sometimes around a shimmering flower or tree, sometimes pure light with no subject at all.
collections.deployFor: AI and creative-technology products, experimental studios, and launches that want to feel futuristic.
collections.risk: Make one luminous organic subject the entire hero's focal point
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] illuminated by blue and warm amber light filaments on a deep navy ground, restrained luminous bloom, dimensional texture, deliberate dark copy space, no text

collections.name: Dark Studio Still Life
collections.description: A real object photographed in dramatic studio light against near-black, with plenty of dark empty space and elegant type. The materials — polished wood, stone, leather — make it feel expensive.
collections.deployFor: Premium physical products, craft makers, hospitality, clubs and luxury shops.
collections.risk: Let the physical subject and its lighting supply all of the page's decoration
collections.imageStyle: premium studio still life of [SUBJECT], tactile natural materials, dramatic soft side lighting, deep dark backdrop, subject on one side and negative space on the other, no text

collections.name: Printed Paper Texture
collections.description: Pages that pretend to be printed: a warm paper-coloured background, the fine dot pattern of old printing (halftone), printers' alignment marks and small typewriter-style data labels.
collections.deployFor: Product sites that should feel crafted, careful and human — tools with a personality.
collections.risk: Render the hero image entirely in halftone dots with visible registration marks
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] rendered as a vintage halftone CMYK print: coarse visible dot grid, slight chromatic misregistration, warm cream paper ground, muted palette with one orange accent, generous soft-sky negative space for headline, flat print finish, no gloss

collections.name: Black-and-White Dotted Photo
collections.description: Stark black and white, with the picture turned into coarse dots and grain like an old screen or photocopy (dithering). The page is split: a form and a strong headline in serif letters (letters with little feet) on one side, the picture on the other.
collections.deployFor: Sign-in, sign-up and waiting-list pages, portfolios and agencies — anywhere holding back reads as confidence.
collections.risk: Dither the entire hero image to 1-bit and let a cropped wordmark run off the viewport
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a stark black-and-white image with heavy 1-bit bitmap dither / coarse film grain, high contrast, dramatic single light source, dark studio or void background, no color, no midtone smoothness - texture must read as deliberate machine processing

collections.name: Vast Misty Landscape
collections.description: One huge landscape photo — mist, fog, dust or a dusk glow — filling the screen, with small, quiet lettering floating in its empty sky. The sheer size of the picture makes the brand feel calm and sure of itself.
collections.deployFor: Brands that must feel serious and trustworthy — large companies, AI and the firms that run computer systems for others — and places or hospitality where the setting is the draw.
collections.risk: Let the landscape occupy 90% of the viewport and shrink the headline to whisper size
collections.imageStyle: vast landscape photograph of [SUBJECT], heavy mist, fog or dust haze, cinematic colour grade (pale fog whites, deep teal dusk or warm golden haze), the upper part dissolving into pale featureless sky or into the page ground for headline space, epic scale, at most one tiny figure for scale, matte photographic finish, not painted or illustrated

collections.name: Pictures Made of Code Characters
collections.description: Pictures built out of the computer's own letters and symbols — clouds and skies drawn in characters (ASCII art), scrambling text, scenes made of tiny blocks.
collections.deployFor: AI and technical products that deserve a showpiece without generic 3D stock art.
collections.risk: Rebuild the hero photo out of the product's own log output or characters
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] constructed entirely from tiny monospace characters (binary digits, ASCII glyphs) varying in density to form the image, characters in amber or blue on a dark teal or white ground, photographic composition but data-native material, crisp legible glyphs up close

collections.name: The Page Is a 3D World
collections.description: The page is a 3D scene you stand inside, drawn live in the browser. Scrolling, dragging or clicking moves you through it — flying over a painted peak, playing with the objects on a desk, travelling from place to place in a story — instead of moving a page down.
collections.deployFor: Showpiece home pages for studios, games, stories and launches, where the feeling of being somewhere matters more than reading fast.
vocabulary: objects that answer hover and click
collections.risk: Replace page scroll entirely with a camera move through the scene, so every section is a place you travel to
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a still frame from a real-time 3D scene: full-bleed environment with depth, soft global lighting, one focal object or landmark lit brighter than the rest, stylised materials (painted or low-poly), camera at eye level as if the viewer stands inside the scene, open area for a small overlaid title, no UI chrome, no text

collections.name: Old Masters Meet Tech
collections.description: Old paintings, statues and engravings set inside a modern tech page, so the old art lends its weight and trust to something new. It comes in two versions. Light: a Renaissance-style painting on a soft sky-blue or white page, with elegant serif lettering (letters with little feet). Dark: a statue, engraving or temple on near-black, broken up by digital glitches, falling characters or a coarse dot pattern.
collections.deployFor: Serious or intimidating fields — law, finance, psychology, crypto — and nightlife or culture brands that want old-world weight.
vocabulary: serif display with italic emphasis word
light variant: soft sky palette, canvas grain, gold accents
dark variant: near-black ground, single hot accent
glyph rain or datamosh glitch over the artwork
collections.risk: Put a 500-year-old artwork behind a live product element — a chat input, a data stream — and let the machine visibly touch the art
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a classical artwork (Renaissance or Baroque oil painting, marble statue or vintage engraving) in one of two treatments. LIGHT: soft sky-blue ground with rolling clouds, warm flesh tones and gold accents, flowing drapery, visible canvas grain, clear negative space on one side. DARK: near-black ground, the artwork corrupted by digital processing (cascading glyph rain, datamosh smears, chromatic aberration or coarse 1-bit dither), one saturated accent colour, dramatic single light. No text

collections.name: Painted Illustration
collections.description: Painted pictures — landscapes, scenes and close-up portraits with visible brush strokes, like gouache (thick watercolour) or a digital oil painting — sometimes with chunky lettering the picture shows through. Warm, human and a little magical, without looking childish.
collections.deployFor: Consumer brands selling warmth, curiosity and delight; fantasy, games and stories; and any page that wants painted background art.
vocabulary: digital-oil portrait with single saturated key light
collections.risk: Mask the entire brand wordmark over the illustrated scene so letters become windows
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a painterly illustration: gouache, animation-background or digital-oil style with visible brushwork, saturated but cohesively graded palette, soft painted light, wondrous but not childish, cinematic composition with a clear calm zone (sky, water or soft painted ground) for type, no text

collections.name: Flat Poster
collections.description: Travel-poster pictures made of flat shapes: a clean line where land meets sky, sky and sea drawn as stripes of solid colour, only a handful of colours, soft rounded outlines. The place is the star; simple shapes do the job a photo would.
collections.deployFor: Travel, places and holidays — brands that want warmth and a sense of somewhere, without using photos.
collections.risk: Let the poster scene carry the whole hero with no photograph anywhere on the page
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a flat-vector travel poster: one recognisable landmark or landscape, crisp horizon, banded sky and water in flat fills, five colours or fewer, organic curved silhouettes, receding layers stepping paler toward the sky, no gradients or texture, open sky band left empty for a headline

collections.name: Soft Hazy Landscape
collections.description: Painted landscapes with few colours, soft edges and little detail that fade into a haze of the page's own background colour, so the picture melts into the page instead of sitting on it in a frame. Far-off shapes turn paler step by step until they nearly match the background.
collections.deployFor: Background art behind a page's words — travel, places, calm or wellbeing brands — wherever the art should set a mood without competing with the text.
vocabulary: atmospheric perspective in stepped value layers
lost edges where shapes share a colour
haze fading into the page ground colour
brightest empty zone reserved for content
collections.risk: Give the art's top and bottom edges the exact colours of the sections around it, so the page scrolls into the scene and out with no visible border
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a soft painted landscape: few colours in one analogous family, soft and lost edges where neighbouring shapes share a colour, detail and contrast draining with distance, far layers stepping paler until they match [PAGE GROUND COLOUR], the brightest emptiest area left where content will sit, fine matte grain, no hard frame edge, no text

collections.name: Mascot Illustration
collections.description: One character or creature as the whole picture, drawn in any style — porcelain, dots, watercolour, patterned ink lines, a starry fill. The character carries the personality; the background stays plain.
collections.deployFor: Brands with a mascot or animal symbol, and any page that needs one friendly figure to hold it together.
collections.risk: Render the brand character in a material idiom (porcelain, ink, stars) instead of its usual flat drawing
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] as a single character illustration rendered in [IDIOM], full figure centred with generous margin, plain untextured ground, fill detail densest at the edges and thinning toward the centre, no text

collections.name: Ink Brush on Bare Paper
collections.description: Black ink brushwork on plain pale paper — a few loose strokes, or a soft ink-wash painting (ink thinned with water), in the style of Japanese ink painting (sumi-e). Most of the paper stays empty; each mark sits exactly where the eye needs it and the viewer fills in the rest.
collections.deployFor: Handmade, natural, calm or heritage brands, and tech pages that want black and white to feel rich without any texture effects.
vocabulary: sparse marks on dominant empty ground
collections.risk: Paint the hero subject in fewer than ten brush strokes and leave the rest of the frame bare paper
collections.imageStyle: [SUBJECT] painted in black sumi-e ink on bare pale paper: a few loose, confident brush strokes or soft ink-wash gradations, dry-brush edges, most of the frame left as empty paper, no colour or one muted wash, no pattern fill, no text

entries.title: Porcelain manta, blue-and-white with gold seams
entries.description: A manta seen from above, made as a blue-and-white porcelain piece in the Dutch Delft style: a white body, cobalt-blue flower and scale patterns packed most densely along the wing edges, dark dots scattered down the middle of the back, and thin gold lines where cracks have been mended (the Japanese kintsugi repair style).
entries.note: Decorate a creature in a blue-and-white porcelain-style pattern, with thin gold lines like mended cracks, and let how dense the pattern is describe the shape: packed tight along the outline, thinning to scattered dots toward the centre.
entries.source: Adobe Firefly, text-to-image, per the file's C2PA manifest
entries.licence: Founder-owned under Adobe's Generative AI Product Specific Terms (21 Apr 2026, output owned by the user, commercial use permitted, not usable as a trademark). The manifest records a reference image fed in; what it was is unrecorded and ownership is assumed (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3086).
entries.image_recipe: A manta ray from above rendered as blue-and-white porcelain: white glazed body, cobalt floral and scale motifs crowding the wing edges and fading to scattered dots on the back, a dotted dark spine line, fine gold repair seams, plain white background, no text.
entries.composition: Centred, symmetrical specimen on plain white: the wings span nearly the full width across the upper half and the tail runs to the bottom edge, leaving the lower corners either side of the tail as the only open zones.

manta.take: The restraint of a single drawing colour on a single background colour, which a version of the mascot could keep. Not the gold: it is a third colour, outside the brand's palette (brand sheet §3).

mmm-infra.take: A decorated sea creature is a mascot piece, and Mark's site has no mascot: the aqueduct logo is its only mark (brand sheet §4).

entries.title: Top picture zooms in as you scroll away; title holds, then leaves
entries.description: A student research site about the Art of Korea gallery at the Metropolitan Museum. The top section is a looping video of layered paper-cut arches, pine sprigs and wave bands in pale blue and grey, under a big white heading ('ART OF KOREA'), a yellow handwritten title and two round buttons, one with a small video of a magpie perched on it. Below come three moon-jar links to the project's parts, a blue 'Be the curator / Share your perspective' band, and a strip of gallery photographs that slides sideways on its own.
entries.note: Make leaving the opening feel like leaning into it: as you scroll away, the opening picture grows slowly and evenly instead of just sliding off, and its words part ways — most scroll off with the page, but the title holds still mid-screen while the picture slides out from under it, and lets go only when the next section's heading rises to meet it. Scroll-driven, so it goes at your pace. Here the picture grows to half as big again by the time it has gone, the held title is handwritten, and further down two lines of a band slide in from opposite sides the first time they come into view.
entries.founder_note: for location hero pages, I like the way the hero enlarges as you scroll down away from it

motion.trigger: scroll (scrubbed, framer-motion useScroll/useTransform + a scrollY listener); secondary: a once-only in-view entrance on the CTA band
motion.range: hero zoom: scrollY 0 → 1 viewport (hero is 100svh; useScroll target=hero, offset ['start start','end start']). Title hold: position:fixed with top=0 until scrollY = 1.02·vh − 230 (688px at 900px tall, 631px at 844px; the code's section[class*='pt-48'|'pt-56'] lookup misses, so the fallback 1.4vh − 0.38vh − 230 applies), then top = threshold − scrollY. The hero section itself is NOT pinned: it scrolls 1:1.
motion.property: transform: scale on the hero <video> (transform-origin center); top on a position:fixed title layer; opacity + translateX on the CTA headlines
motion.from_to: video scale 1 → 1.5, linear in scroll (measured 1.222 at 400px, 1.444 at 800px, clamped 1.5 from 900px); title text box stays at ~324px from the viewport top (±3px from an 8 s SMIL 'breathing' of its two textPath arcs, sag 280↔268 in a 1000×600 viewBox) until 688px, then moves 1:1 with the page; 'ART OF KOREA' h1 and the two 110px circles move 1:1 (no parallax); CTA headlines x −80px→0 and +80px→0, opacity 0→1
motion.duration: zoom and hold: scrubbed; CTA slide-in 1800 ms (delays 300/450 ms); hero text entrance 1200 ms; hover circle colour flood 750 ms; gallery strip is a separate 20 s linear infinite CSS loop, not scroll-linked
motion.easing: zoom and hold: linear (scrubbed, no spring); CTA slide-in cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); hover flood cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
motion.purpose_note: the hero picture zooming in as you scroll away from it while the handwritten title holds mid-screen until the next section meets it — for location hero pages
motion.reduced: no reduced-motion handling: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the zoom (1.222 at 400px), the title hold and the 20 s strip loop all run unchanged

manta.take: Worth trying on each location's page: the destination scene behind the hero zooms in slowly as the visitor scrolls away, while the place name holds still mid-screen until the first section of content arrives, then scrolls on with it. Zoom only the scene, not the ink wave band and mascot in front of it (§8). Because it follows the scroll rather than running on a timer, it does not fight the brand sheet's quick-motion rules (§10); leave out the site's timed slide-ins (1.8 s) and hover colour flood (0.75 s), which run far longer than the sheet's 120–180 ms.

mmm-infra.take: A way to leave the opening without a second animation: once the aqueduct is built, scrolling away makes its arches grow slowly while "MMM Infra" holds still until the first section reaches it, all at the reader's own pace. Not the handwritten yellow title, the magpie video button or the gallery strip that slides on its own, which are the kind of busyness Mark disliked on MacGeorge's site (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: A still hillside where only the grass, mist and one bird move
entries.description: Product page for CoolDock, a Mac app that adds a second Dock of live widgets. The top of the page is a wide landscape of green rolling hills in hazy sunrise light, melted into the pale page at top and bottom, under a heavy black headline, with two large boulders in the foreground and a Mac screen mock-up rising between them. The landscape is a six-second looping video in which almost everything stays still; hovering a boulder makes moss spread over it where the pointer passes.
entries.note: Make a scene a living picture rather than a video: most of it stays perfectly still — often the parts further away — while only the few things that would really move in that place move on their own, small and natural, with quiet gaps between. Because so little moves, you notice each movement a moment late, so the picture feels alive rather than like a film playing. Here it is a still hillside where only the near grass sways, a puff of mist drifts across the foot of a hill, and once a loop a bird flies in towards you; soft fades at top and bottom melt the scene into the page, so it has no frame.
entries.founder_note: home and hero pages could have a tiny bit of animation to make it feel alive. Maybe wind gently rustling elements, a bird flying across the sky, or the manta logo swimming.

motion.trigger: autoplay loop while the hero is in view and the tab visible (IntersectionObserver); nothing is scrolled or hovered
motion.range: hero only: a 1440×800px video band starting 150px from the page top, object-fit cover, blended into the page colour by a 454px top and a 350px bottom gradient; the same video plays again behind the footer; no scroll link
motion.property: pre-rendered footage (H.264 1280×720, scene-optimized.mp4; below 810px a 960×540 scene-mobile.mp4 with the same content); the page itself animates nothing in the scene
motion.from_to: camera locked (phase-correlation shift 0px across the loop); sky and far hills static (mean frame difference ≤ 3.6/255, compression noise); near-slope grass (lower left) sways continuously; a mist puff forms at the left foot of the middle hill ~1.5–2 s, drifts right and thins by ~5.5 s (mean difference up to 22/255 there); one dark bird of prey enters left at ~2.5 s (x≈240, y≈376 of 1280×720), climbs to y≈290 and exits right at 6.0 s, its size growing ~15× and its speed rising from ~50 to ~800 px/s as it flies towards the viewer
motion.duration: 6.03 s loop; the video fades in over 1 s (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) on load
motion.easing: none declared: natural motion in the footage; the loop seam cuts the bird at the right edge, then ~2.5 s of empty sky
motion.purpose_note: a still landscape with a few living parts — grass swaying, mist drifting, one bird crossing — so the page feels alive without playing like a film
motion.reduced: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (also prefers-reduced-data, Save-Data, or a 2g/3g connection) pauses the video and shows the still poster (data-cd-media-mode=static)

manta.take: For the home and destination heroes: keep most of the illustrated scene still — usually the parts further away — and let two or three things that would really move there move on their own: grass or palm fronds stirring, a bird crossing now and then, the manta swimming along inside the ink wave band (§8) — with long quiet gaps between. The brand sheet's motion rules (§10) only cover hover and press, so a small ambient loop nobody triggers needs its own line there, and it should stop when a visitor has asked for reduced motion, as this site does.

mmm-infra.take: The kind of video Mark likes, made calm: behind the homepage, a mostly still picture of real infrastructure (a bridge, a dam, a viaduct) where only water, cloud or a far vehicle moves, with long quiet gaps, so the page feels alive without playing like a film. A short looping clip of this kind is Kling 3.0's job (brand sheet §7). Not the app-store chrome: the heavy black headline, the black download buttons and the screen mock-up between boulders sell a product, not a person.

entries.title: Misty forest darkens and dissolves into a glass pavilion as you scroll
entries.description: Home page of Izanami, a company built around Japanese ideas of harmony, with a school, a craft line and retreats, and offices in Dubai and Tokyo. It opens on a full-screen photo of a misty pine forest with one line, 'Remember who you are', a logo top left, a language switch and menu top right, and two live clocks (Dubai and Tokyo) along the bottom. Scrolling down, the forest dims to near-black and a photo of a glass pavilion in a misty garden comes up out of the dark; the same fade to dark later carries the pavilion into a dark list of the three projects.
entries.note: Move from one scene to the next so gradually that there is never a moment when one picture replaces another: the first scene barely moves and fades out in place while the next is already waiting underneath, and the two are chosen or drawn to share a colour where they overlap, so for a moment you see both at once. Nothing slides over the top and there is no edge — one setting simply turns into the other, which feels natural rather than like an effect. Here a misty forest dims towards near-black over a glass pavilion whose dark ceiling lines up with the forest's dark lower half, so the trees show faintly through the roof before only the pavilion is left.
entries.founder_note: the way that the above page fades as you scroll is nice

entries.title: Flyward — map-island reveal, coastline section edges, a gold trail drawn by scrolling
entries.description: Flyward is a travel-management company's home page. It opens on a sunset terrace photo seen through an island-shaped hole in a white page ruled with faint map lines, and scrolling widens the hole until the photo fills the screen. Further down, each section's picture meets the next along a torn, coastline-like edge, and a winding gold line draws itself between four numbered photos as you scroll.
entries.note: Three ideas that make scrolling feel like travelling. Open on a shape that first reads as a flat pattern or texture, then grow it as you scroll until it becomes a window onto a full scene that makes sense — a small, pleasant surprise. Let sections meet along organic, natural-looking edges instead of straight lines. And draw a path that fills in as you scroll, winding like a trail between the stops on the page rather than running straight down. Here the shape is an island cut out of a white page ruled like a map, the edges are torn like coastlines, and the path is a thin gold trail between four numbered photos — choices that suit a travel company; another site would pick a shape, an edge and a path that fit its own story.
entries.founder_note:
the way scrolling zooms you in, and then the whole scrolling and section transition system is beautiful. Do this with a manta ray on an ink sea scene for my home page? Maybe also in transitioning from cards to hostels' individual pages: the card enlarges and becomes the page. Section borders and transitions could be good for our about and guide pages.

entries.title: EverSwap — flying over a painted peak into the valley behind
entries.description: EverSwap's home page is one painted 3D landscape filling the whole screen: sharp green peaks under a blue sky, with the name in large thin serif letters standing in the scene. The page itself never scrolls; the mouse wheel, a finger drag or the arrow keys move a camera along a set route — up over the peak and down into the valley behind it, over rivers seen from above, then across a lake toward a range of peaks — while each part's words fade in and out over the scenery. Five small diamonds on the left edge (along the bottom on a phone) mark the parts.
entries.note: Move the viewer through the scene instead of moving the page: scrolling carries you around the thing in front to reach what is behind it, as if you were physically there. It feels real rather than like a cheap effect when everything a real journey changes, changes together — near things sweep past faster than far ones and uncover what is behind them, something passes close in front, distant parts go soft in haze, the light shifts as you go, and a slight sway keeps it from feeling like a ride on rails. The other thing worth keeping is the full-page painted art style. Here a camera rises toward a painted peak, the site's 3D name and a bird pass the lens, and the view tilts over the ridge and drops into the valley behind, across one hand-painted landscape that fills the screen edge to edge.
entries.founder_note: perhaps a too-complicated version of above, but I like the idea of going around a front page object to reach the page physically behind. Also, I like this full-page aesthetic art style for the home page as an option.

entries.title: Khufu's — a living, dust-hazed desert scene that melts into the page
entries.description: A restaurant site at the Giza pyramids. Past its opening text screen, the home page is a full-screen film, looping every 10 seconds, of the pyramids in a sandstorm haze, with a camel and its handler walking slowly across a dune beneath a large line of thin capitals. The film's lower third melts into a flat sand colour that the next section carries on; further down, the background drifts from sand to white, and then from white to dark brown as you scroll through the closing section.
entries.note: Make a scene feel faded and almost dreamlike with haze that is alive: dust, mist or cloud drifting slowly through a mostly still picture, colours kept pale with no true darks, and the bottom of the scene fading into the page's own background colour so it has no edge. If the scene is a short loop, restart it at its quietest, haziest moment so the jump never shows. Here it is a 10-second film of the pyramids in drifting sandstorm dust, with a camel and its handler slowly swallowed by it, under a faint warm veil that melts into the sand colour of the next section — and the page keeps fading after it, sand to white to dark brown as you scroll.

entries.title: Eagle's Nest — footer links step aside for a growing dot
entries.description: The footer of a concept site for a yoga and dance retreat on Lake Atitlán, Guatemala: a deep bottle-green panel with the address top left, a column of eight menu links in a large serif in the middle, social links top right, and "EAGLE'S NEST" across the full width at the bottom in cream. Pointing at a menu link grows a small cream dot at its left while the word slides a short way right to make room; the social links and the credit only dim slightly. As you scroll into it, the footer stays still and the cream page above slides up off it.
entries.note: Make a link physically make room when you point at it: a small mark grows in at the start of the line and the word slides aside to clear space for it, both together on a fast-then-settling curve, and both slide back when you leave. Because the word keeps its shape and only moves, it feels like an object being nudged rather than text being restyled; keeping everything around it quiet lets that one movement read clearly. Here, in a dark green footer, a cream dot grows beside each menu word while the word steps right by about a letter's width, mostly there within a sixth of a second.

entries.title: GROWON — a home-screen desk scene you play with; the record player plays music
entries.description: A Korean web studio's home page that is one 3D scene of a desk floating on a dusky blue background: a monitor, a record player, a mug, a notebook and pencil, a leather office chair, a potted plant and a floor lamp. While it loads ("Setting the scene…") the objects drop onto the desk one after another. The page does not scroll: a two-line headline sits bottom left, a sound button top left and a menu top right, and every object in the scene reacts when you point at it or click it.
entries.note: Make the home-page picture something to play with: the objects people would naturally reach for answer when you point at them or click them, with a small movement or a sound, so the picture feels like a little real place rather than a flat image — and one object can switch the page's music on and off. Pick those objects with care: if everything reacted, the scene would feel cluttered and confusing. Here it is a 3D desk scene where every object reacts: the record player's arm swings onto the record and a song fades in, the lamp switches the room to night, the chair swivels, the pencil rolls off the desk, the whole scene leans slightly toward the mouse, and some objects double as the menu.

entries.title: Nomadic Tribe — a narrated journey where each place flows into the next
entries.description: An interactive new-year story by the studio makemepulse (2019). A narrator tells how a tribe leaves the island it tended for a year, says goodbye at a waterfall, flies across the ocean at night on the backs of giant birds, and lands at dawn on a bare sandy island where the first flower blooms. It plays in four full-screen illustrated 3D scenes inside a drawn frame, with spoken narration and subtitles, background sound for each place and music; each scene asks one small action before a Next button appears, and the page never scrolls.
entries.note: A feel built from travelling rather than from the drawing style: move between places by passing through something from the scene itself instead of cutting, let sound carry half the atmosphere, and go at a slow, one-thing-at-a-time pace where each place asks one small, clearly named action. Moving the mouse shifts the view a little, so each place feels like somewhere you are standing. Here it is a four-chapter story: the camera tips into a bush, rolling clouds or a sand dune to reach the next place, a narrator and the sounds of each place play, the music adds a layer each chapter, and the cursor names the one gesture — Drag, Click or Hold.

manta.take: The journey feel, not the drawing style: moving between places by passing through something drawn from the place itself — a wave, rice-field grass, cloud off a volcano — instead of a cut; and a quiet, optional sound layer of the place, off until the visitor turns it on. The brand's motion rule (brand sheet §10: quick, never announces itself) covers the working area; a scene-scale transition would belong only in the hero/marketing zone (§2), and never gate the search behind a gesture or a narrated wait (§1: energy never costs a search).

mmm-infra.take: A narrated story that makes the reader drag, click or hold before it lets them on is a wait and a piece of bespoke software, where a brochure site gives a busy reader Mark at once (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Pink cliffs fading into cream haze above a sand-coloured beach
entries.description: A painted cove seen from above: striped rose-pink cliffs with a pine on top, a rock stack beyond, a turquoise wave curling onto a wide pale beach, and one small figure carrying a green surfboard. The paint is dry and grainy (streaky on the cliffs and sea, speckled on the sand) and there are almost no drawn lines. The sky runs from pale blue at the top to an almost white pink at the horizon.
entries.note: Let art live in the page it sits on: keep almost the whole picture in the page's own pale background colour, repeat far shapes in paler and paler versions until the farthest is nearly that colour, and let shapes thin out at their base so they melt into the ground instead of ending at a hard edge. Texture can then do the work of lines. Here pink cliffs step back into cream haze above a beach that is simply sand-coloured space, painted in dry, streaky strokes with no outlines inside the shapes — and the beach-and-surfer subject is itself one of the feelings Manta should give off.
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A cove seen from above in dry, grainy gouache with a collage feel: rose-pink cliffs with horizontal dry-brush strata and an umbrella pine on the ridge, a second paler cliff and a rock stack behind it, each further shape repeated in a paler pink until the far headland is nearly cream (#F5E6E7); the stack fades to cream at its base as if low sea mist sat on the water; a broad turquoise wave with streaky brush texture and white foam curling onto a wide speckled pale-sand beach (#EADBCA–#E0CEAF) that fills the lower half; one small figure carrying a patterned green surfboard; sky pale blue (#C7E3E4) at top fading to near-white pink (#F6F1F1) at the horizon; no outlines on the landscape, no text.

manta.take: Take the fade-to-sand: a picture that already sits almost entirely in the page's own pale sand, its far shapes fading into it and thinning out at their base, so it seems to rise out of the page rather than sit on it. The beach-and-surf subject is on-message too, one of the feelings Manta should give off. The dry, streaky paint texture is worth trying in the background-art trials (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A painted holiday beach with a surfer says leisure travel, and the site's pictures are to be refreshed from Mark's own, possibly his LinkedIn posts, not from holiday art (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Temple face at dawn, jungle palms fading step by step into sky
entries.description: A carved stone face tower of the kind found at Angkor fills the centre-left against an apricot dawn sky with a pale sun disc. A broadleaf tree with a red trunk stands on the left; on the right, palms and jungle recede in paler and paler layers into a misty grey-green, with a few small white birds. The stone is painted in flat lit and shadow shapes, with dark cut lines for block joints and carvings.
entries.note: Name a place with one landmark's outline and build everything else from silhouettes that step back into the air: each layer further away is paler and closer to the sky colour, so a few simple shapes give real depth. Let the light do the romancing — warm at the top, cool at the bottom, with the landmark catching both. Here a carved temple face tower says 'Angkor' from across a room, while palms and jungle beside it fade step by step into a misty dawn.
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.

entries.composition: Near-square crop with the face tower filling the centre-left from the bottom edge almost to the top; the sun disc sits top right in the only open sky; the right third holds the receding palm and jungle layers that fade into mist; the bottom is carved stone steps with a small seated figure, not mist.

manta.take: Take the jungle and the landmark together: palms and forest as plain silhouettes that pale step by step into the sky suit Indonesian jungle and temple scenes, and one landmark, such as a Balinese temple gate, names the place. Try the landmark both ways, as an outline alone and with its carved detail: how much detail background art can carry is for the trials to show, and so is the sky fading from one colour into another (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A tourist poster of a temple face at dawn; the only landmark this site names is its own aqueduct, and Mark's pictures are to come from his own work (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Pink stag drawn without a single line, shaped by grainy shading
entries.description: A pale pink stag stretched upward with its head thrown back and its legs trailing, as if mid-leap, over a fan of spiky teal and mint leaves around a dark teal disc, on plain white. The stag has no outlines: its body is shaped by soft, speckled shading from pale pink to coral, and the eye is only a faint pink mark.
entries.note: A creature, or any iconic subject, can read at a glance with no drawn lines at all: its outline plus soft shading, from light to shadow through a fine grain, does all the work, and the grain adds a faint paint texture for free. Setting the smooth body against spiky shapes makes it feel softer still. Here it is a pink stag mid-leap over a fan of spiky teal leaves, with no eye, mouth or leg lines drawn.
entries.source: Dribbble, saved as `dribbble1.jpg` into the founder's `brand_assets` folder; the shot and its author are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A pink deer leaping with its head thrown back, smoothly airbrushed, over a radiating fan of angular dark-teal and mint leaf shapes with a stippled edge, plain white background, no outlines, no text.
entries.composition: Near-square spot illustration on white: the stag leaps on a diagonal from lower right to upper left across a centred dark-teal disc, with no open background zones, so it sits beside text rather than behind it.

manta.take: Take it as a model for drawing the creatures and landmarks in Manta's art — the manta, and the other animals and scenes a destination calls for: one smooth outline, no inner lines, and form from a soft, grainy shift of tone, so each reads at a glance but stays quiet. Its pale-peach-and-teal pairing is already close to Manta's peach and turquoise. Leave the white ground and the dark disc, which make it a sticker rather than a scene. The grainy shading is worth trying in the background-art trials (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A decorative leaping stag is a spot illustration with no place on a site whose one mark is the aqueduct logo (brand sheet §4).

entries.title: Steam rising into a sky of soft, rounded cloud shapes
entries.description: An illustration of a rust-and-ochre geothermal plain with steam vents, a rope-fenced path and a small figure in red holding a staff, seen from behind. Steam from the vents rises into a turquoise sky piled with rounded, scalloped clouds drawn with thin outlines. The ground is busy with mottled colour and outlined pebbles; the sky, which fills nearly half the picture, is far calmer.
entries.note: Make a calm sky from soft, rounded shapes with no sharp corners, and join sky and ground with one element that turns from one into the other. Keeping the sky's lines hair-thin and close to the sky's colour lets it stay quiet above a busier ground. Here steam leaves the vents with no outline and gains thin outlines as it climbs, until it becomes the lobed clouds; a small figure on the path, back to you, gives the scale and puts you on the walk.
vocabulary: unlined steam merging into outlined cloud
entries.source: Jon Juarez (illustrator), saved as `jon-juarez-home.jpg`; the page it came from is not recorded.
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.

entries.composition: Portrait crop with the horizon just below the middle; the upper half is cloud, lighter but line-textured (type needs a scrim), the figure stands dead centre on the path, and the busy rust-and-blue foreground fills the bottom third.

manta.take: Take the sky: rounded, lobed cloud and steam shapes for the upper part of a page, and the idea of one element, such as the steam from Bromo's or Ijen's crater, flowing up into the sky. Try the detailed ground and its fine outlines too: how much detail, and how many colours, background art can carry is for the trials to show (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A comic-book fantasy landscape in saturated turquoise and rust, far from the calm site Mark wants for development-bank staff (brand sheet §1).

entries.title: Sunlit valley whose far end dissolves into a sand-coloured glow
entries.description: A painted mountain valley with the sun low at its far end: a tall rock spire and cliffs lit warm on the left, a sheer wall in blue-grey shadow on the right, water and trees on the valley floor, and long streaks of peach and grey cloud overhead. It is painted in broad, flat brush strokes with visible edges and no drawn lines.
entries.note: Make art fade into the page with light: put the brightest, emptiest part of the scene where the content will sit, make that glow the page's own background colour, and let everything grow darker and more detailed only toward the edges. Detail drains away with distance as well as contrast, and the place is romanticised by the glow rather than recorded. Here the sun sits in the gap at the far end of a valley, each cliff lighter and flatter than the last, until the gap is almost exactly a pale sand colour.
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A wide mountain valley backlit by a low sun sitting in the gap at its far end, painted in broad, flat, angular brush strokes with visible edges: a tall spire and cliffs on the left lit warm, a sheer wall on the right in cool blue-grey shadow (#3D4449), water and trees on the valley floor, long horizontal peach and grey cloud streaks; cliffs step lighter, warmer and flatter with distance (#615452 → #9C8A82 → #DBAB94 → #FACE9E) until the gap is sand-cream (#FBF5E5) with almost no internal contrast; no outlines, no text.
entries.composition: Widescreen crop with a low horizon in the bottom quarter; dark cliffs frame both edges, the low sun and brightest haze sit centre-right, and the pale upper-middle sky is the open zone for type.

manta.take: Take the glow as a way to make art fade into the page: put the brightest, emptiest part of a scene where the content sits, let that part be the page's own sand, and have the land step darker only toward the edges. The loose painted brushwork is a style to try; your own list names painterly styles (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A romantic painted canyon at sunset is game concept art, not a picture that helps a reader judge Mark, whose images are to come from his own work (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Boardwalk starting at your feet, sky made of flat pink stripes
entries.description: A boardwalk with wooden railings starts at the bottom edge and bends through long green grass and pink flowers toward a green-topped headland, a small pinkish beach and a blue sea. The sky is one flat turquoise with flat pink cloud strips that crowd into a solid pink band along the horizon; two small birds fly across it. It is painted as flat colour shapes without outlines.
entries.note: Three ideas. Start a path at the viewer's feet and bend it away into the scene, so the eye walks in and you feel already on the way. Make a soft, hazy horizon without any blending: flat stripes of a pale colour that get thicker and closer together until they merge into a solid band. And build every surface from visible brush-stroke shapes in flat paint, so the picture feels hand-painted yet stays clean. Repeating one colour near and far ties it together. Here a boardwalk starts at the bottom edge and bends through grass toward the sea, under a flat turquoise sky whose pink cloud strips crowd into a pink band on the horizon; the grass is layered blades in three or four greens and the flowers are single pink dabs.
vocabulary: colour echo (pink repeated near and far)
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A wooden boardwalk with slim railings starting at the bottom edge and bending left then right through long green grass and pink flowers toward a green-topped headland, a small pinkish beach and a mint-to-blue sea; sky one dead-flat turquoise (#9BDEE6) with flat pale-pink cloud strips (#F8DDE2) that thicken and crowd together into a solid pink band on the horizon; the same pink repeated in the boardwalk planks, beach and flowers; two small birds; flat colour shapes with crisp edges, grass as flat stroke shapes in three or four greens, no outlines, no gradients, no text.
entries.composition: Portrait frame with the horizon at roughly one-third height from the top; the boardwalk enters bottom-centre and leads to a mid-right headland, leaving the banded sky across the top third as the clear text zone.

manta.take: Take all three. The flat-stripe haze gives a soft, hazy horizon with no blending. The path — a walkway or jetty that starts at the viewer and leads toward the destination — suits a page's lower edge, kept simple behind the cards. And the painted finish, every surface built from visible brush-stroke shapes, grass as layered blades and flowers as single dabs, is a clean, hand-painted look worth trying in the background-art trials (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A seaside boardwalk travel print in turquoise and pink says holiday, and the site's pictures are to be refreshed from Mark's own (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Blue valley in seven layers, each paler until it meets the sky
entries.description: A painted mountain valley in blues: dark conifers and grey boulders at the front, then ridge after ridge in paler blues, up to snowy peaks almost the colour of the pale sky. A waterfall drops from a gap at the centre, where white mist fills the valley, and a thin river winds from it toward the viewer. A patch of bright green meadow at the lower left is the only other colour.
entries.note: Build depth from many layers of one colour family, each a simple silhouette a step paler than the one in front, until the farthest nearly matches the sky, and let detail drop away with distance too. It shows how many steps of haze a scene needs and how to space them, and one bright point gives the eye somewhere to rest. Here about seven layers of blue run from near-black pines to pale peaks, forest turns to streaks and then to bare slopes, and a misty waterfall at the centre is the bright point.
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: An alpine valley in one blue family built from about seven stacked silhouette layers that go paler toward a flat pale-blue sky (#DBF1FE): near-black conifer spires and grey boulders at the front corners (#082022–#1D3030), ridges at #376C99, #5C94B3, #6AB4D0, a tall right-hand wall #58A1CE, far snow peaks #C1E6FB with white dab highlights; mid-slope forest reduced to vertical paint streaks, far slopes treeless; a waterfall dropping from a misty white gap at the centre, a thin pale river winding from it toward the viewer, one bright green meadow patch lower left; soft painted edges, no outlines, no text.
entries.composition: Landscape frame with peaks filling the upper half and a V-shaped valley converging at lower centre; the pale sky strip at top-left and the washed-out peaks give the only low-contrast zone for text, and the dark conifer corners frame the bottom.

manta.take: Take the layer count and the rule that detail drops with distance; in Manta's scenes the far layers would fade into the sand page rather than a blue sky. Try the soft painted edges, and a version with each layer as one flat shape beside it (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059). Use the near-black front trees with care behind listings, where your principles put the cards first and suggest exploring low contrast.

mmm-infra.take: If the aqueduct is built in a setting, the valley an aqueduct crosses can be drawn this way: a few layers of one colour family, each paler than the one in front, until the farthest is almost the page's ground, with the logo's grey arches as the one firm shape before them (brand sheet §6). Not the snowy fantasy peaks, the waterfall or the near-black pines in front, which would fight the arches for the eye.

entries.title: Fisherman poster where shapes melt into the sand and sea
entries.description: A poster-style picture of a bearded man in a navy smock, cap and white trousers leaning on a pole in the left foreground; behind him are a pale beach with two boats, two small figures running along the shore, and white chalk cliffs topped by a tiny house. It is built from a few large flat shapes with soft, airbrushed fades and no outlines. There is no horizon line: the sea and sky run together in one blue with soft pale streaks.
entries.note: Economy and lost edges: build figures and places from a few large shapes, and let neighbouring shapes share colours so their borders disappear — no outline where one thing meets another, not even a horizon line between sea and sky. A few soft, rounded shapes can stand for a whole surface. Here a fisherman's face is two orange shapes and a beard with no eye drawn, his white trousers fade into the pale sand, and rounded pools and one long shadow say 'wet sand' without detail — romantic in the way of an old holiday poster.
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A mid-century travel-poster scene: a bearded man in a navy smock (#1F304F), flat cap and white trousers leaning on a pole in the left foreground, face as two flat orange planes and a navy beard with no eye drawn; behind him a warm pale beach (#FEDEAF) with a white-and-blue boat and an orange rowing boat, two small figures running along the shore, white chalk cliffs with a green top, a thin zigzag path and a tiny house; sea and sky one blue with soft pale streaks and no horizon line; rounded blue tide pools and a long flowing cast shadow on the sand; large flat shapes with soft airbrushed fades where shapes meet (white trousers melting into the sand), no outlines, no text.
entries.composition: Portrait frame with the figure filling the left half from head to knee; the beach, bathers and cliffs sit small on the right, and the upper-left sky beside the figure's cap is the only open zone for text.

manta.take: Take the lost edges and the soft, rounded pool-and-shadow shapes: art that fades into the sand page where it meets it instead of ending at a hard border, with shapes kept to a few large pieces. The airbrushed fades are worth trying (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059). Behind a results page keep any person small, like the two on the shore: a big foreground figure pulls the eye from the cards.

mmm-infra.take: A nostalgic seaside poster of a fisherman; the person this site shows is Mark himself, in real photographs (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: One warm colour family, one temple tower on a dune
entries.description: A near-empty desert scene: one smooth dune curving across the lower half, a small stepped temple tower peeking over its ridge, and a pale sun disc in an apricot sky. Everything is in one warm family of sand and apricot tones; the only strong dark is the shaded side of the tower. The dune has a faint paper texture with fine fibres in it, and a sparkle of tiny dots runs along the ridge where the light catches the sand.
entries.note: A picture calm enough to sit behind a page: nearly everything in one warm colour family, sky and ground so close in brightness it looks seen through haze, and the only strong dark given to the one thing that names the place — one landmark over one simple curve is enough. A faint texture finishes it: a paper grain over everything and a sparkle of fine dots where the light catches an edge. Here a small temple tower peeks over a single dune under an apricot sky, and the sparkle runs along the dune's ridge.
vocabulary: one dark accent on the landmark
entries.source: Dribbble, saved as `dribbble2.jpg` into the founder's `brand_assets` folder; the shot and its author are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A minimal desert scene in one warm tonal family: a smooth sand dune curve across the lower half, a small stepped temple tower just breaking the ridge, its shadowed face the only dark value in the picture and a thin pale rim of light along its sunlit edges, a pale sun disc with a soft glow in the upper right, a flat apricot sky, a faint paper-fibre texture on the dune and a fine stipple sparkle along the ridge line, no outlines, no text.
entries.composition: Landscape frame with the dune curve rising from left and falling right at roughly mid-height, the tower small at centre on the ridge and the sun top-right; the upper-left sky and the flat dune foreground both stay empty for text.

manta.take: Take the low contrast and the single landmark: art in one warm colour family, pale enough to sit behind cards, with one Indonesian landmark (a temple gate or a volcano, say) as the only strong shape. Its apricot sky is warmer and darker than the page sand (sand-page, brand sheet §3), so it would be lightened toward it. The faint paper grain is worth trying in the background-art trials (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A calm stage for the opening animation on the muted ground Mark floated (brand sheet §2): nearly everything in one quiet colour family, sky and ground close in brightness, a fine paper grain over all, and the only strong dark given to the aqueduct as it is built. Not the temple tower, the sun disc or the hot apricot: Mark has chosen no colour yet, and the arches are the logo's grey.

entries.title: River seen from straight above: one boat on a colour fade
entries.description: A wooden boat seen from directly overhead, just left of centre in the lower half, with one rower in a conical hat and blue top pushing an oar. The rest is open water, shown only as a smooth fade from gold at the top to olive-green at the bottom, with no ripples drawn. A soft dark shadow of the boat shows under the surface, and a scatter of pale specks spreads from the oar blade.
entries.note: A quiet, matte style: smooth colour fades softened by a fine grain, with small, cleanly drawn subjects shaded in the same grain, so the whole picture feels soft and calm rather than glossy. It suits looking straight down, where water has no horizon and one fade can fill the picture, given a few small clues — something floating, its soft shadow, a little spray. Here a lone rowing boat, small and off-centre, sits on a gold-to-olive river with a spray of pale specks at the oar.
entries.source: Dribbble, saved as `dribbble3.jpg` into the founder's `brand_assets` folder; the shot and its author are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).
entries.licence: No licence held — private reference only. Never published, reproduced or shipped on a Manta surface.
entries.image_recipe: A wooden sampan seen from directly overhead, just left of centre in the lower half of the frame, one rower in a conical hat and blue top pushing a long oar; the rest of the frame is open water drawn only as a smooth vertical fade from warm gold at the top to olive-green at the bottom, no ripples; a soft, blurred dark shadow of the boat under the surface, offset below it; a small spray of pale speckles where the oar blade meets the water; fine grain, no outlines, no text.
entries.composition: Landscape frame with the boat set diagonally just left of centre in the lower half; the entire upper half and the right third are unbroken water, clear for text.

manta.take: Take the overhead view and the matte, fine-grained style: seen from above, water has no horizon, so a soft colour fade can fill the whole area behind a results list while one small subject names the place — your own example of swimming with manta rays is this picture with a manta gliding under the surface in place of the boat. The grainy fade is worth trying in the background-art trials (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A rowing boat on a river is a travel vignette with nothing to say about Mark or his work (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Soft painted lake scene in muted teal, cream and peach
entries.description: A painting of snow peaks behind a still river, dark blue-green pines on the left, a peach-coloured tree on the right, dusty peach and plum-brown scrub on both banks, and a muted teal sky with cream and peach clouds. The brushwork is loose and dabbed with no drawn lines; the peaks are two tones, light and shade, and the far treeline fades into a pale haze.
entries.note: A soft, loosely painted landscape with every colour turned down, so even cool against warm stays gentle: far shapes fade into pale haze, forms are just light and shade, and no lines are drawn, so it stays calm and romantic rather than busy. Here it is snow peaks over a still river, with deep blue-green pines, peach foliage and a greyed teal sky.
vocabulary: muted teal, cream and peach palette
entries.source: Founder's `brand_assets` folder; the original artist and the page it was saved from are not recorded (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3042 sorted the folder without provenance).

entries.title: Desert band whose sky and ground match the page around it
entries.description: A wide flat-colour desert illustration on the Studio Wanderwell home page (studiowanderwell.com, loaded 29 Sep 2026; the image file is named 'Roadtrip'): a dark green cactus at the left with its shadow, a terracotta dune with a white road running to a half-set apricot sun, a cream sky and a pink foreground. It is a still image placed between two page sections. Its sky is the same cream as the section above it, and its pink foreground the same pink as the section below, where the heading 'What makes us different' begins.
entries.note: Make an illustration part of the page rather than a picture placed on it: give its top edge the exact colour of the section above and its bottom edge the exact colour of the section below, so as you scroll you pass into the scene and out again without crossing an edge. The picture needn't move; the matched colours do the work. After that, a quiet picture of a journey, a road running off toward the sun, and simple flat shapes in warm colours. Here a desert band between two sections has a cream sky matching the section above, a pink foreground matching the one below, and a white road running off to a setting sun.

entries.title: Canyon seen from the rim, a river winding off into pale distance
entries.description: A canyon seen from high on its edge: striped red rock walls stand at both sides, and a pale blue river winds from the bottom of the picture across an orange valley floor dotted with small blue-green shrubs. The colours fade from deep red and orange close by to pale lilac and blue on the far flat-topped hills, under a blue sky of rounded cream clouds that trail off into thin streaks. There is no text.
entries.note: Give a picture miles of depth with colour alone: strong, warm colours close by, paler and cooler ones further away. A route winding away from the viewer adds the sense of a trip still ahead, and a bold, sunny travel-poster look makes it feel open and adventurous. Here red canyon walls give way to an orange valley floor and pale lilac hills, and a river starts wide at the bottom edge and narrows as it winds away.
vocabulary: atmospheric perspective by colour: saturated warm near, desaturated cool far
winding river leading line, widening toward the viewer
terraced strata drawn as contour strokes
scalloped cumulus trailing into streak lines

entries.composition: Portrait frame with the horizon at about 40% from the top, rock walls cropping both side edges and the river winding up from bottom-centre; the cloud-banded sky in the top third is the text zone.

manta.take: Take the depth made from colour: near shapes strong and warm, far shapes paler and cooler, which lets a picture of a volcano or a bay of islands feel huge with only a few colours. It is also the one scene in this group with no building at all, the place told by its landform alone, which is how many guide pages will have to work.

entries.title: Standing on the Great Wall, its warm path winding off ahead
entries.description: A portrait travel print: the Great Wall starts at the bottom edge as a paved walkway and winds right and up past watchtowers with curved red roofs to a far peak, while blue ridges edged with thin pale yellow-green lines fall away on the left under a teal sky and cream clouds. A white margin under the picture carries the words 'CHINA / THE GREAT WALL'.
entries.note: Put the viewer on the path: start the route at the bottom edge, where you would stand, and let it wind off toward the place, making it the one warm thing in a cooler picture so the eye follows it without trying. Draw layered hills as flat shapes with only the sunlit top edge picked out in a thin pale line, and rock and buildings as bold, crisp poster shapes with a hard split between light and shadow, so they feel solid and dramatic; a neat place name beneath finishes it as a travel print. Here the Great Wall's walkway winds up past red-roofed watchtowers toward a far peak, its bricks drawn as small lit blocks, the cliffs as dark jagged planes with rounded teal tree clumps clinging to them.
vocabulary: first-person path from the bottom edge
warm accent path in a cool field
receding ridge layers with rim-lit crest lines

entries.composition: A portrait poster with the wall rising from bottom-centre to a peak at upper right and valleys receding at left; the sky's upper-left third is the open zone, and the title sits on a white plate below the art.

manta.take: Take the path at your feet: a guide-page picture that begins on the trail, boardwalk or temple steps and leads off into the place makes the visitor feel already on their way, and a warm path through a cool scene leads the eye with no arrow needed. mmm-infra.take: Though its subject is a great built structure, this is a tourist print with a souvenir caption, and the site's pictures are to be refreshed from Mark's own work (brand sheet §6).

entries.title: Red sun, snowy Fuji and a pagoda, like an old worn print
entries.description: A small image (194 by 259 pixels) of a Japanese scene: a big red sun behind the snowy peak of Mount Fuji, a tall tiered pagoda with warmly lit windows on the right, a pine on the left, and red and orange autumn trees along the bottom. A pale band of mist lies between the mountain's foot and the trees. It is all in muted red, ochre and grey-teal on paper that looks worn and scratched, darker at the edges and in the top-right corner.
entries.note: Tell a place with two or three shapes everyone knows, stacked one behind another, each drawn the way that place would draw it, so even the shapes feel local. An old printed-keepsake finish, faded inks on worn paper, makes it feel like a treasured souvenir. Here Japan is a red sun set right behind a snowy Fuji, echoing the flag, with a pagoda in front, every shape reading as Japanese. The saved image is tiny, so only the overall look carries.
vocabulary: stacked national icons: sun disc, volcano, pagoda
large red sun disc behind the peak
mist band separating middle ground from foreground
muted brick, ochre and grey-teal palette

entries.composition: Portrait frame with the sun disc and peak in the upper-left half and the pagoda rising along the right third; the foliage fills the lower third densely, leaving only the textured sky strip at the top for text.

manta.take: Take the stacking: two or three shapes anyone recognises for the place, layered front to back and each drawn so it feels unmistakably of that place, which is also your idea that each destination's icon be 'something that represents that destination'. The worn paper and faded inks are worth trying as a texture in the background-art trials (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A Japanese travel keepsake in faded red and ochre on scratched paper says holiday souvenir, not an advisor to development-bank staff (brand sheet §1); its worn paper is not one of the grounds Mark floated.

entries.title: Clear turquoise channel between sunlit village houses
entries.description: A narrow channel of water between village houses: rocks and cream-and-white houses with orange roof edges on the left, taller sunlit houses with balconies on the right, and two small boats moored along the right-hand rocks. The channel runs back to a small bay with boats and a far shore under a blue mountain. The water fills the lower half, drawn as interlocking flat patches of deep teal, bright aqua and pale mint, mixed with the warm colours of the houses reflected in it.
entries.note: Draw water with no lines at all: puzzle-like flat patches in several blues and greens, broken by streaks of the colours around it, read as clear, gently rippling water. Seen from low at the water's edge it invites you in, and the whole feels like a hot, bright summer day with water clear enough to jump into. Here it is a channel between sunlit village houses, looking up it to the open bay.
vocabulary: broken reflections as interlocking flat patches
warm sunlit walls with cool blue shadow faces
channel vanishing point to an open bay

entries.composition: Portrait frame with buildings walling both sides and the inlet running to a horizon just above centre; the sky in the top quarter is the only open zone, and the reflective water fills the lower half.

mmm-infra.take: A bright holiday harbour painted in turquoise patches sells a summer break, which nothing on a calm site for development-bank staff needs (brand sheet §1).

entries.title: Sunset old town with a shadow skyline behind it
entries.description: Luxembourg's old town at sunset: a big pale-yellow sun in a flat orange sky, the cathedral's tall dark spires rising into it, and cream, white and yellow houses with dark slate roofs on a ridge between two dark green tree masses. Behind them a second skyline of towers and roofs is cut out in an orange a shade deeper than the sky, and a brick viaduct with nine dark arches runs the full width across the front above a band of teal water. Flat colour throughout, with no texture.
entries.note: How little it takes: one colour for the whole sky, a sun and a handful of recognisable shapes, and a place is still unmistakable. A second skyline behind the first, cut out in a colour only a shade deeper than the sky, makes the place feel bigger without adding detail, and one warm colour over everything gives a quiet storybook evening. Here it is a town of roofs, spires and arches under a single orange sky, with a deeper-orange skyline behind.
vocabulary: large sun disc with landmark tip rising into it
tone-on-tone shadow skyline behind the lit subject
monochrome orange sky with faint arcs

entries.composition: Portrait frame with the sun upper-centre, the town mass centred at mid-height, and the viaduct spanning the full width across the lower quarter above a thin teal river strip; the orange sky around the sun is the open text zone.

Take too the band across the foot of the picture as the destination-art version of the hero's ink wave (§8).

mmm-infra.take: The brick viaduct across the foot: a row of arches drawn as a few flat shapes, with no texture, is how the aqueduct could stand in the opening animation and still read at once as the logo's arches (brand sheet §4). Not the orange sunset, the storybook town or the sun: Mark has chosen no such colour (§2 is open) and the opening is about the aqueduct alone.

entries.title: St Peter's at golden hour, doubled in a long pool
entries.description: St Peter's Basilica at the far end of a long, straight approach, lit gold, with white rays and a pale glow spreading from behind the dome into a teal sky of gold and cream clouds. Ochre palaces and tall cypress trees line both sides and small figures walk along the paths. A long rectangular pool with stone edges runs down the middle toward you, holding the dome's upside-down reflection in wavering gold patches.
entries.note: Make the picture an arrival: a symmetrical view where every line runs to the one famous thing, so you feel you are walking straight up to it, bathed in warm light at the best hour of the day. A reflection at your feet, showing it a second time, adds to it. Here the pool's edges, the paths and the rows of cypress all lead to a great dome in golden light, reflected upside down in the pool.

entries.composition: Portrait frame with the dome centred just above mid-height, buildings walling both edges, and the reflecting pool filling the lower third; the teal-and-gold sky in the top third is the open zone, though busy with cloud.

manta.take: Take the arrival view: a straight approach, such as a jetty, a temple stairway or a path between rice terraces, leading to the one landmark makes a guide page feel like getting there. Leave the sunburst rays behind, which lucmoseley/mantahostels#3148 called 'sunburst theatre'.

mmm-infra.take: A golden-hour tourist poster with sunburst rays is grand and theatrical, the opposite of the plain, approachable personal advisor (brand sheet §5).

entries.title: One pagoda under a big sun, ghost temples in the hills
entries.description: A tall red tiered pagoda, which looks like Hanoi's Tran Quoc pagoda, stands dead centre with its tip rising into a big pale-yellow sun on a peach and pink sky, with small white seated figures in its arched openings. A palm is silhouetted on the left; behind, layered teal hills hold faint outlines of another tower and a curved gate roof, crossed by a pale band of mist, with lime-green banks fading to darker green in front. Across the bottom run a dark red shore line and bands of teal and sage water with pointed streaks and faint reflections.
entries.note: Tell a place simply: one landmark you would know at once, standing straight up into a big soft sun, one plant to say the climate, and nothing else competing. Let the colours do the rest: a warm sky over cool land, with the landmark in the warmest colour set right against the coolest, so it glows. Faint outlines of more landmarks in the hills, a shade lighter than the hills, hint there is more to find without clutter, and the same style could serve every place. Here a red-orange pagoda rises from teal-green hills into a peach-pink sky with a pale yellow sun, a palm beside it and yellow-green bushes along the water.
vocabulary: centred vertical landmark rising into the sun disc
tone-on-tone ghost silhouettes in the middle ground

manta.take: Take the one-landmark portrait: a single shape that says the place, the temple, volcano or surfboard of your destination-icon idea, standing tall against a big sun, with flat water bands across the bottom; and its colour, a warm sky over cool land with the landmark in the warmest colour against the coolest. The soft colour fades on the banks and sky, and the light grain, are worth trying too (lucmoseley/mantahostels#3059).

mmm-infra.take: A tropical pagoda poster in peach and pink is travel art for a holiday, with no place on a calm site for development-bank staff (brand sheet §1).

entries.title: Weir and pool where every stroke shows the water moving
entries.description: A landscape-format painting of a river weir: a wide curtain of water pours over it and tumbles through coral-orange boulders into a turquoise pool, with smaller falls on the right below a stone cottage on a walled bank. Behind, a person walks a small dog along a path under trees, against lime and yellow fields. Big leaves and a leafy sprig are cut off by the bottom edge, and everything is hand-drawn in crayon-like strokes in very bright colour.
entries.note: Make water look alive in a still picture by letting the strokes follow how it moves: straight down where it falls, long sweeping curves where it spreads, tight loops where it foams, so you can almost hear it. Bold, bright colour makes it a lively summer day, and framing it from the bank behind big leaves puts you there, looking in. Here it is a waterfall into a turquoise pool between coral rocks and lime fields.
vocabulary: directional mark-making: vertical strokes on falls, sweeping arcs on the pool, scribble loops for foam
high-chroma complementary palette: coral against turquoise
tiny figure with dog for scale
